Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consistent adjective

unchanging, true to oneself

also consistently, consistency, inconsistent, be consistent

classical

Cic. Off. 3.35: rēcta et convenientia et cōnstantia nātūra dēsīderat (Lewis & Short, s.v. conveniō)

cōnstāns, cōnstantis

adjective, third declension

steady, consistent, unchanging

Of a person or a course of action that stays the same; cōnstantia is consistency. It also means firm, steadfast.

Other words

  • sibi cōnstāre — to be consistent, stay true to oneself

    phrase: cōnstō, cōnstāre with the dative of the reflexive · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 60 (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnstō)

    “To agree with oneself”: of a person, a speech or an argument. The adverb cōnstanter is “consistently”.

  • aequābilis, aequābile — even, uniform, consistent

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.111 (Lewis & Short, s.v. decōrus)

    Even, the same throughout; aequābilitās, evenness of life and conduct, is Cicero’s word.

Examples

  • omnīnō sī quicquam est decōrum, nihil est profectō magis quam aequābilitās ūniversae vītae

    if anything at all is becoming, nothing surely is more so than consistency in the whole of one’s lifeCic. Off. 1.111 (Lewis & Short)

  • in Oppiānicō sibi cōnstāre et superiōribus cōnsentīre jūdiciīs dēbuērunt

    in the case of Oppianicus they ought to have been consistent with themselves and agreed with the earlier verdictsCic. Clu. 60 (Lewis & Short)

See also consistent, regular.

SourcesLewis & Short: consto · Lewis & Short: aequabilis · Lewis & Short: decorus
